title: Activate CPU encoder backend descriptor selection
summary: Activated only descriptor-backed EncoderBackend=cpu selection for encode attempts while leaving hardware AV1/NVENC, QSV, and AMF backend overrides fail-closed.
reason: Encoder breadth remediation needed a narrowly bounded backend activation step that can use existing validated CPU fallback mechanics without prematurely enabling unvalidated hardware backends.
behavior_before: EncoderBackend round-tripped through settings and diagnostic reports, but normal encode activation still ignored it. AV1/NVENC primary stayed inactive, while AV1 CPU behavior was reachable only through explicit CPU fallback or CPU-primary libaom selection.
behavior_after: EncoderBackend=cpu now resolves the configured VideoCodec family to its CPU descriptor, passes readiness and attempt evidence through descriptor activation, skips the hardware ladder in Do-Encode, and uses the existing CPU fallback attempt shape. Explicit EncoderBackend=nvenc preserves only literal active HEVC/H.264 NVENC selections; AV1/NVENC, QSV, AMF, and codec-family override activations remain blocked.
tests_added: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-EncodeFlagPolicyChecks.ps1 covers EncoderBackend=cpu readiness/plan behavior plus NVENC/QSV fail-closed assertions.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-EncoderCapabilityProbeChecks.ps1 covers EncoderBackend=cpu descriptor activation evidence in capability reports.
